catalogue.shared_across_zones:
I did not take the surveys' word for which types are shared. I parsed all 70 files in build/auto-extract myself, then parsed the 25 act_tbl arrays in build/audit/source/src/R*/ACT*.C and resolved every record through its own round-and-act table (ACTION.C:53 dispatches act_tbl[actno-1]). That turns 242 per-round id slots into 177 distinct retail routines, which is the real count of distinct object types across all seven zones. 60 is the count of distinct raw id values, and it is meaningless: ids are per-round.

Thirteen routines appear in 3 or more rounds. Counts are placements across all 70 programs, then the ids they wear per round:

spring 3936, all 7 rounds, id 10 everywhere.
ring 3934, all 7 rounds, id 16 everywhere.
item 2120, all 7 rounds, id 25 everywhere.
friend (animals) 1836, all 7 rounds, SIX different ids: R1 36, R3 57, R4 47 (as friend4), R5 45, R6 41, R7 40, R8 50.
ball (spin/speed tag) 1236, 4 rounds: R1 52, R3 53, R6 30, R7 43.
shooter (tube transport) 370, 4 rounds: R1, R5, R6, R8, id 7 everywhere.
marker 260, all 7 rounds, id 19.
mosugu 84, all 7 rounds, id 22.
goal 72, all 7 rounds, id 23.
bigring 64, all 7 rounds, id 20.
et (robot generator) 60, all 7 rounds, ids R1 45, R3 55, R4 81, R5 46, R6 46, R7 41, R8 67.
movie (projector) 48, 6 rounds, ids R1 46, R3 56, R4 82, R5 44, R6 47, R7 39. R8 has no projector at all - there is no MOVIE8.C and no movie entry in any ACT8*.C, so Metallic Madness buys its Good Future from et alone.
gene (capsule) 10, 5 rounds, id 21. R7 and R8 Act 3 place no capsule.

Only three more routines reach even 2 rounds: bobin (286, R3 id 29 + R8 Act 3 id 29 - ACT83.C includes ../R3/BOBIN.H), dango (80, R7 42 + R8 45), togeball (44, R3 44 + R6 45). Everything else is single-round.

The number that decides build order: 23,224 placements live outside Palmtree Panic. 9,082 of them (39%) already sit on an id whose port handler is the right object. 9,886 sit on an id the port binds to a DIFFERENT object and would mis-spawn. 4,256 sit on an id the port does not know and would be dropped. 104 (round, id) pairs collide. Worst: R6 id 34 is dair6 (546 platforms) but the port spawns a badnik; R7 id 40 is friend (544) but the port spawns a springboard; R4 id 52 is wall1 (504 solids) but the port spawns a spin tag; R5 id 48 is dair5 (498 platforms) but the port spawns Amy's heart.

ranked.name: ring (RING.C)
ranked.rounds: all seven, id 16 in every act_tbl
ranked.rationale: The one shared type I could prove needs zero behaviour work. RING.C:149-165 ringtbl is byte-for-byte the DELTAS list at tools/convert_objects.py:8, all 16 entries, and no round uses a high nibble above 11, so the port's run expander is already correct for every ring record on the disc. Counts per round: R3 582, R4 338, R5 542, R6 616, R7 650, R8 572. Two converter fixes needed, not object code: 38 R8 ring records carry a non-zero secondary byte and tools/convert_objects.py:18 raises on them.

ranked.name: spring (SPRING.C)
ranked.rounds: all seven, id 10 in every act_tbl
ranked.rationale: Subtypes observed per round: R3 {0,2,4,6,8}, R4 {0,2,4,6}, R5 {0,2,4,8,10}, R6 {0,2,4,6}, R7 {0,2,4,6,8,10}, R8 {0,1,2,4,6,8,10}. Every one is inside the port's existing bit decode at src/objects.c:178-186 (bit1 weak, bit2 horizontal, bit3 diagonal). This type alone unseals one of the 18 sealed programs: the stall report's R82B lift is a spring at x=431 y=1112 sub 1 Past-masked, which I confirmed in objects82A.bin.

ranked.name: item - monitor and time post (ITEM.C)
ranked.rounds: all seven, id 25 in every act_tbl
ranked.rationale: Every round uses subtypes 0-9 only, inside the port's sub>9 reject at src/objects.c:169. R4 402, R8 352, R6 314, R3 238, R7 264, R5 224. Without the time posts no zone can change era, so this is the type that makes the other six zones a Sonic CD rather than a Sonic 1. Same converter secondary-byte fix as ring: 8 R8 item records carry d=1.

ranked.name: friend - the animals (FRIEND<n>.C)
ranked.rationale: Highest placement count of any type that needs a real decision, and the decision is only which id. Subtypes are {0,1} in every single round, which matches the port's (sub&127)>1 reject at src/objects.c:158 exactly. R7 544, R5 308, R4 260, R3 216, R6 186, R8 52. R4 links FRIEND4.C and R8 splits sheep/hato rather than pocky/inco, so the art differs per round; the roam-and-ground-follow code transfers unchanged.

ranked.name: ball - spin tunnel / speed tag (PLAYSUB.C)
ranked.rationale: I read src/objects.c:678-697 and the port ALREADY implements all five subtypes including the ball_rd7 pad branch (2,3,4) that R1 never places. R7's 784 placements use exactly subtypes 0-4, R3's 274 and R6's 68 use 0 and 1. The only gap is one constant: PLAYSUB.C:873 raises the horizontal floor from 2560 to 3328 when stageno.b.h==5, which is Wacky Workbench, and the port hardcodes 2560. Note R7 id 43 is ball in Acts 1-2 and wall73 in Act 3, so the map has to be per-act, not per-round.

ranked.name: marker - checkpoint star post (PLAYSUB.C)
ranked.rounds: all seven, id 19 in every act_tbl
ranked.rationale: Subtype is the checkpoint ordinal and runs to 8 in R8, 6 in R5 and R7; the port passes it straight to scd_player_checkpoint() at src/objects.c:213, so no bound is violated. Present-only in every round, which I confirmed from the era masks rather than assuming. Small count but it is what makes a death in a new zone survivable.

ranked.name: wall1 - static sized solid (R4/WALL1.C) - R4 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R4 only (collides with R1 id 52 = ball)
ranked.rationale: Best value per line in the whole catalogue. build/audit/source/src/R4/WALL1.C is 138 lines and the entire object is: patno = subtype, sprhsize/sprvsize = tbl0[subtype*2..+1] over 7 sizes, then hitchk(pActwk,&actwk[0]) every frame. 504 placements, and the stall report proves R42A/B/C/D are sealed at x=661 without it - I confirmed the three stacked records in objects42A.bin at x=320 y=400 sub5, x=448 y=1040 sub5, x=384 y=1680 sub5, bridging a terrain column with no solid pixels. Four of the eighteen sealed programs for one tiny object.

ranked.name: wall7 - static sized solid (R7/WALL7.C) - R7 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R7 only (collides with R1 id 36 = friend)
ranked.rationale: R7/WALL7.C is 95 lines, the same shape as wall1: six half-sizes from wall7_tbl0, hitchk every frame. 460 placements, subtypes 0-5. No stall proves it load-bearing (no R7 Act 1 or 2 program stalls at all), but 460 solid blocks is genuine level geometry that is simply absent today, and the port would currently spawn animals at every one of them.

ranked.name: mosugu - goal approach sign (GOAL.C)
ranked.rounds: all seven, id 22, subtype 0 only
ranked.rationale: Exactly one per program in six of seven rounds. Subtype 0 everywhere, so the port's handler needs nothing but the id map and the lifted zone gate. Grouped with ranks 10-12 as the act-end set: together they are 180 placements for what is effectively four table entries.

ranked.name: goal - end-of-act signpost (GOAL.C)
ranked.rounds: all seven, id 23, subtype 0 only
ranked.rationale: One per program in Acts 1 and 2 of every round. Without it no non-Palmtree act can end. Note the port's naming is inverted relative to retail: SCD_OBJ_GOAL is 22 (retail mosugu) and SCD_OBJ_SIGN is 23 (retail goal). The ids are right, the labels read backwards.

ranked.name: bigring - Special Stage ring (GOAL.C)
ranked.rounds: all seven, id 20, subtype 0 only
ranked.rationale: One per program past the signpost in Acts 1 and 2. Subtype 0 in all seven rounds. The port already deletes it once the matching time stone is held; only Special Stage 1 exists in this prototype, which caps the payoff but not the cost.

ranked.name: gene - animal capsule (GOAL.C)
ranked.rounds: five (R1,R3,R4,R5,R6), id 21, subtype 0 only
ranked.rationale: Only 10 placements in the whole game and 2 of them are R1's, but it is the Act 3 end condition for four more zones. R7 and R8 Act 3 place no capsule record at all, which I verified directly - their boss acts end some other way, and I did not determine how.

ranked.name: wall73 - Act 3 sized solid (R7/WALL73.C) - R7 ACT 3 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R7 Act 3 only (same id is ball in R7 Acts 1-2)
ranked.rationale: 166 lines, reuses wall7_tbl0 sizes plus an optional scripted path that only 2 of the 56 records use. Stall-proven: R73C and R73D free-fall at x=12790 through a 128px hole, and I confirmed the exact record in objects73C.bin - id 43 subtype 3 at x=12224 y=496, which wall7_tbl0[6..7] makes a 128x32 solid whose top is y=480, the same as the floor either side. Two more sealed programs for one small object.

ranked.name: et - robot generator (ET<n>.C)
ranked.rationale: Eight placements per round, subtype 0 everywhere, and it is the sole Good Future switch in R8 (which has no projector). The port's generator already gates on the Past and awards the flag at src/objects.c:1196-1202. Pure id-map work, with the caveat that the id moves in all seven rounds and R5/R6 both land on 46, which is the port's projector.

ranked.name: dair6 - oscillating rideable platform (R6/DAIR6.C) - R6 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R6 only (collides with R1 id 34 = ene_kamemusi)
ranked.rationale: The largest single-round structural type in the game and DAIR6.C is only 155 lines: displacement is sin(gametimer & 255) * 4 >> 4 from the spawn point, subtype 0-3 picks right/left/up/down, 48x24, one sprite frame, ridechk each frame, horizontal variants write their own delta into the rider's xspeed. Every instance in the zone swings off the global frame counter, so there is no per-instance state to model.

ranked.name: beem6 - electric arc and flash trigger (R6/BEEM6.C) - R6 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R6 only (collides with R1 id 33 = dodai platform)
ranked.rationale: 364 placements and every single one carries subtype 0, which BEEM6.C:84 makes inert after init. A draw-only 32x32 stub plus one global flash controller covers 100 percent of the records. Cheapest way to make Wacky Workbench look like itself. The R6 survey flagged that 364 copies of an inert decoration is odd enough to want a capture to confirm, and I agree - the code says inert, nothing I read contradicts it.

ranked.name: togedair8 / harir8 - spike and spike-block (R8/TRAP_R81.C) - R8 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R8 only (collides with R1 id 54 = kowasi breakable wall)
ranked.rationale: 386 placements, second largest in R8. Subtype bit 7 splits it: 248-255 are the spike and block forms, 0 and 1 are a 32x32 block that spawns a spring or a spike child 24px above itself. No ridechk anywhere in it, only hitchk, so nothing stands on it - it is a hazard, not geometry, which is why it sits below the platforms despite the count.

ranked.name: konbea - segmented conveyor belt (R8/KONBEA.C) - R8 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R8 only (collides with R1 id 42 = kasoku ramp)
ranked.rationale: Only 104 placements but stall-proven for four programs: R81A/B/C/D sit in a 225-cell sealed pocket and I confirmed the two konbea records inside it in objects81A.bin at x=487 y=1840 and y=1916, era mask 7. KONBEA.C is 961 lines and builds a chain of 16x10 segment children driven along a 446-point path table, so the cost is real; the payoff is four of the eighteen sealed programs.

ranked.name: piston - sine lift and rider launcher (R8/PISTON.C) - R8 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R8 only (collides with R1 id 52 = ball, and with R4 id 52 = wall1)
ranked.rationale: 201 lines, and the subtype is a clean bitfield: bits 0-1 shape, 2-3 speed from {4,8,16,32}, 4-5 starting phase from {0,256,512,768}, 6 radius, 7 launch strength. ride_on_chk carries the player and shape 1 fires the rider at yspeed -4096. Stall-proven for R82A, R82C and R82D; I confirmed the record in objects82A.bin at x=432 y=1182 era mask 6 and its Present-only sibling at x=321. R82B's Past uses a spring in the same slot, so spring already covers that fourth program.

ranked.name: dair5 - moving platform and conveyor (R5/DAI_RD5.C) - R5 ID SPACE
ranked.rounds: R5 only (collides with R1 id 48 = heart1)
ranked.rationale: 498 placements, the most of any stall-proven type, and it seals four programs: R51C/D and R53C/D. I confirmed the R51C record at x=320 y=400 subtype 3 Future-masked. The cost is why it ranks here and not higher: 594 lines, a 25-entry subtype table setting pattern and half-width, parallel belt_flag and bane_flag tables, six movement modes, conveyor push whose speed is era-dependent (0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 px per frame by time_flag) off a global colrevflag that a separate switch object (beltsw5, id 49, 172 placements) owns, plus spring children spawned onto the platform surface. Quartz Quadrant is not cheap and should be scheduled as a zone, not as a type.

ranked.name: shooter - tube transport (SHOOT<n>.C)
ranked.rounds: four (R1, R5, R6, R8), id 7 in every act_tbl
ranked.rationale: Shared id and shared mechanism - it seizes the player (actfree[2]=129, mstno 2, speeds zeroed) and drives him waypoint to waypoint - but the data is not shared at all. The port's tunnels.inc holds Palmtree Panic's 3 paths and src/objects.c:165 rejects any subtype above 2. R5 declares shooterpositbl[22], R6 nineteen paths with subtypes up to 138, R8 thirty-nine subtype values from 128 to 188. Each round needs its own path table extracted before a single record spawns, which is why 358 placements rank this low.

ranked.name: movie - Metal Sonic projector (MOVIE<n>.C)
ranked.rationale: Eight placements per round, Past-masked, subtype 0. The port's projector_step carries a hardcoded four-child table and a 12-step explosion script from projector.inc, both derived from R1/MOVIE1.C, so each round needs its own child offsets and art. Low count, but with et it is half the Good Future condition in five zones. Skip it for R8, which has no projector object.

catalogue.disagreements:
I checked the contradictions against the data rather than averaging them. Eight are real.

1. ALREADY_IMPLEMENTED, R5 against the other six. R5 marked all 28 of its types false. R1, R3, R4, R6, R7 and R8 marked the shared ones true. Both describe something real and the flag is being used for two different questions. Verified: 36 distinct object types have working handlers in src/objects.c, all at Palmtree Panic's ids (I resolved the 41 entries of supported_types[] through ACT11A/11B/12A/13C and they cover exactly R1's 36 placed ids). And src/objects.c:34, `if(objects_zone)active_placement_count=0`, means zero placements from the other six rounds reach any handler. So "a handler exists" is true, "it runs for this zone" is false everywhere but R1. I counted already_implemented as 36 on the first reading.

2. TIME POST POLARITY, R5 against R4. R5 says ITEM.C:288-292 makes subtype 8 set time_item = 1 (Past) and 9 set it to -1. R4 says 8 is -1 and 9 is +1. Read build/audit/source/src/ITEM.C:288-293: `if (userflag.b.h != 8) { time_item = 1; sub_sync(118); } else { time_item = -1; sub_sync(119); }`. R4 is right. R5 has the sign inverted; its Past/Future labels are right, so the error is cosmetic, but anyone porting t_item off the R5 text would send the player the wrong way.

3. GETROUNDSTR, R5 against R7. R5 says it "lives in the Windows executable and is not in the decompiled source (it is only called)". It is in the source, at build/audit/source/src/LOADER2.C lines 35-56, and it is the cleanest era proof anyone found: time_flag 0 writes 'B', 1 writes 'A', 2 writes 'C' when generate_flag is set and 'D' otherwise. So Past='B', Present='A', Good Future='C', Bad Future='D', and era-mask bit0 = time_flag 0 = Past. R7's citation is correct and this independently confirms the bit assignment all seven surveys derived by other routes. No survey got the era bits wrong.

4. R3's SECONDARY BYTE. R3 states flatly "it is 0 in all 4006 R3 records". There is one distinct record with d=255: objects31A-D at x=4544 y=890, id 36 (ene_kama), subtype 255 - four placements. It matters because id 36 is in convert_objects.py's SUPPORTED set, so line 18 raises ValueError('unsupported secondary subtype') on it.

5. R8's SECONDARY BYTE, and this is the one with teeth. R8 says d is non-zero on 40 records, only on ids 47 and 35. The real figure is 114 placements: id 16 ring 38, id 25 item 8, id 35 bigbom 40, id 47 scarab 28. The ring and item ones sit on the two types the first slice builds, and both ids are in SUPPORTED, so convert_objects.py:18 aborts the R8 conversion before it emits anything. Fix the guard before the slice, not after.

6. DENOMINATORS. R1 says "byte 7 is non-zero only on two Act-1 records"; I count 8 R1 placements. Not a contradiction - R1 counted distinct records, I count placements across the four era programs, which are byte-identical files. Several surveys switch between the two conventions inside one entry. Every headline count in this catalogue is placements across all 70 programs. Divide Act 1 and 2 figures by 4 and Act 3 by 2 for distinct records.

7. BALL'S SPEED FLOOR. R3 writes "3328 in zone 5", R6 writes "round 6". PLAYSUB.C:873 is `if (stageno.b.h == 5) cal_speed1 = 3328` and Wacky Workbench is stage index 5. Same fact, two numbering schemes. R6's reading is the useful one.

8. UNSORTED LAYOUTS. R6 flagged objects63C/63D (records 65 and 66 run x 2568, 2567, 2566) and warned convert_objects.placements(ordered=True) would raise. True. R1 did not mention that its own objects13C/13D are unsorted too - record index 56 is x=3056 after x=3088. That one is already handled: tools/convert_objects.py:139-141 calls placements(ordered=False) for Act 3 with a comment explaining that native streaming spawns by distance, so record order only sets slot order. R6 Act 3 needs the same treatment, and the pattern is a known one rather than a defect.

Where the surveys AGREE and I confirmed it: every per-round total and distinct-id count reproduces exactly from the binaries - 4062/36, 4006/31, 3208/46, 3476/28, 3420/35, 6006/28, 3108/38, summing to 27286 across 242 (round, id) slots. All 21 four-file and two-file era groups are byte-identical, so era selection is entirely the byte-6 mask. The 8-byte >HHBBBB layout and the field meanings from ACTSET.C:325-362 are consistent across all seven.

BLOCKS_TRAVERSAL is the column I trust least and the surveys knew it. R1 and R6 set all entries false and said why. R3, R4, R5, R7 and R8 set a handful true from their own terrain probes. The stall report is the only arbiter that actually moved a player, and it names five types across eighteen sealed programs. Nothing stalls anywhere in R3, in R6, in R4 Act 1, or in R7 Acts 1-2, so the traversal claims in those surveys - R3's frip, drumr3, for3 and frdr3, R4's awa, sw4, tobira4 and tobiras4, R7's chgban - are plausible but uncorroborated at any specific x. I did not decode terrain myself and I am not overriding them; I am saying they carry less weight than the five the walker proved.
catalogue.stall_conclusion:
Eighteen of the twenty-six stalls are missing objects, eight are the bot, and there are zero terrain defects. I verified the object side of every one of the eighteen by pulling the cited records out of the binaries myself.

The eighteen reduce to just FIVE distinct object types, and one of those is already implemented:

wall1 (R4 id 52) seals R42A, R42B, R42C, R42D. Confirmed in objects42A.bin: id 52 at x=320 y=400 sub5 Present, x=448 y=1040 sub5, x=384 y=1680 sub5, stacked across a terrain column with no solid pixels.
dair5 (R5 id 48) seals R51C, R51D, R53C, R53D. Confirmed in objects51C.bin: id 48 subtype 3 at x=320 y=400, Future-masked, hanging 240px above flat ground.
konbea (R8 id 42) seals R81A, R81B, R81C, R81D. Confirmed in objects81A.bin: two records at x=487 y=1840 and y=1916, era mask 7, inside the 225-cell sealed pocket.
piston (R8 id 52) seals R82A, R82C, R82D. Confirmed in objects82A.bin at x=432 y=1182 era mask 6 and x=321 y=1182 Present-only.
wall73 (R7 Act 3 id 43) seals R73C and R73D. Confirmed in objects73C.bin: subtype 3 at x=12224 y=496, and wall7_tbl0 entry 3 makes that a 128x32 solid whose top is y=480 - the exact height of the floor on both sides of the 128px hole.
R82B is the eighteenth, and its lift is a SPRING: objects82A.bin id 10 subtype 1 at x=431 y=1112, era mask 1 (Past). The port already implements springs. That program comes unstuck the moment the zone gate opens.

So four new objects, three of them small, plus a type the port already has, clear every proven stall in the game.

The eight bot stalls are not data problems and should not enter the build queue. tools/zone_walk_test.c presses Jump for exactly one frame, and Sonic's jump is variable height, so the walker only ever hops 33px against a real 100px full jump. R41A-D, R43C/D and R83C/D are all inside that gap; the report measured held-jump variants clearing them with zero objects spawned. Fixing the walker is a one-line change that removes eight false blockers from the board and should happen before anyone reads another stall list.

One caveat I am carrying forward rather than resolving: the report itself flags R51C/D and R53D as its weakest calls, because the terrain step there is a steep quarter-pipe face that is inside jump range on paper. The dair5 record hovering in empty air at exactly the needed height is strong circumstantial evidence, not proof.
catalogue.recommended_first_slice:
Do NOT start by lifting src/objects.c:34. Measured: of the 23,224 placements outside Palmtree Panic, opening the gate with the port's current flat id table would spawn the CORRECT object for 9,082 of them, the WRONG object for 9,886, and silently drop 4,256. 104 (round, id) pairs collide. A naive gate lift makes six zones worse, not better.

THE SLICE. One piece of infrastructure plus ten types, none of which needs new object behaviour:

Infrastructure: a per-ROUND-and-ACT id-to-handler table, replacing the assumption that type ids are global. Per-act is not optional - R7 id 43 is ball in Acts 1 and 2 and wall73 in Act 3, R3 id 48 is a cutscene barrier in Act 1 and a boss part in Act 3, R8 id 29 is a beam in Act 2 and R3's pinball bumper in Act 3. Then lift the gate.

Types, all already implemented at Palmtree Panic's ids, needing only the map and in two cases one line:
ring 16 (3300 unlocked), spring 10 (3222), item 25 (1794), friend 36 to 40/41/45/47/50/57 (1566), ball 52 to 30/43/53 (1126), marker 19 (228), mosugu 22 (64), goal 23 (56), bigring 20 (52), gene 21 (8).

That is 11,416 placements, 49 percent of everything outside Palmtree Panic, for an id table, one subtype check, and one constant.

The two lines: PLAYSUB.C:873 raises ball's horizontal floor from 2560 to 3328 in Wacky Workbench and the port hardcodes 2560; and the animals need a per-round species check because R4 links FRIEND4.C and R8 splits sheep/hato.

Three converter fixes go in the same slice, and they will abort the build if they do not. tools/convert_objects.py:18 raises on any non-zero secondary byte outside ids 7 and 42 - that hits 38 R8 ring records, 8 R8 item records, 1 R3 record (x=4544, id 36, d=255), 52 R4 screw, 68 R5 denden and 48 R6 block6. Six of the seven rounds abort on it. placements(ordered=True) raises on objects63C/63D; apply the ordered=False pattern already used for R1 Act 3 at line 141. And check capacity as you go: the worst fully-expanded program is R7 Act 2 at 965 placements against SCD_PLACEMENT_CAPACITY=1024, so there are 59 slots of headroom and no more.

WHAT I VERIFIED SO THE SLICE IS SAFE. The ring run expander needs no change at all: RING.C:149-165 ringtbl equals tools/convert_objects.py:8 DELTAS entry for entry across all 16 rows, and no round uses a high nibble above 11. Springs never exceed subtype 12 in any round, all inside the existing bit decode. Items never exceed subtype 9 in any round, inside the existing reject. Animals are subtype {0,1} in all seven rounds. Ball subtypes are 0-4 and src/objects.c:678-697 already implements all five, ball_rd7 branch included. The four act-end objects are subtype 0 in every round. Nothing in the slice needs a subtype I could not account for.

THE SECOND SLICE, once the first proves out: wall1 (R4 id 52, 138 lines, 504 placements, unseals R42A-D), wall7 (R7 id 36, 95 lines, 460 placements) and wall73 (R7 Act 3 id 43, 166 lines, 56 placements, unseals R73C/D). Three static sized solids totalling under 400 lines of retail C, 1,020 placements, and six of the eighteen sealed programs. Every one of them is "read a size from a table, call hitchk" - the cheapest real level geometry in the catalogue.

Then the four zone-shaped commitments, in cost order: dair6 (R6, 546), konbea and piston together (R8, 208, four more sealed programs), and dair5 with its beltsw5 switch and global colrevflag (R5, 670). Leave shooter and the bosses alone until a zone actually needs them.

errors_found: CONVERTER FIX LIST INCOMPLETE (build-breaking): the catalogue's recommended_first_slice lists the convert_objects.py:18 secondary-byte hits as '38 R8 ring, 8 R8 item, 1 R3 record, 52 R4 screw, 68 R5 denden, 48 R6 block6' (=215). Recounted against the actual guard (line 17 skips kinds outside SUPPORTED before the check; line 18 exempts kind 7/42 when secondary==1), the real raising set is 254 placements: R3 id36 4, R4 id53 52, R5 id32 68, R6 id42 44, R6 id62 12, R8 id16 38, R8 id25 8, R8 id47 28. It OMITS R6 id 62 (12 placements, R6 Act 3, secondary 5/6/7) and R8 id 47 (28 placements, R8 Act 1, secondary 1 and 10) entirely, both of which are in convert_objects.SUPPORTED and will abort the conversion.
R6 id 42 OVERSTATED: catalogue says '48 R6 block6'. Four of the 48 carry secondary==1, which convert_objects.py:18 explicitly exempts for kind 42. Only 44 raise.

'Six of the seven rounds abort on it' is FIVE. Aborting rounds are R3, R4, R5, R6, R8. R1's only non-zero secondaries are kind 7 and kind 42 with secondary==1 (both exempt). RING.C ringtbl matches DELTAS row for row, and the ITEM.C, PLAYSUB.C:873, LOADER2.C and ACT83 citations are all accurate. Thirteen defects survive. The most serious is operational: the recommended first slice's converter fix list is wrong in three ways and would abort the build it was written to protect. It omits R6 id 62 (12 placements) and R8 id 47 (28 placements) although both are in convert_objects.SUPPORTED, and it overstates R6 id 42 by 4 because secondary==1 is exempt for that kind. The real raising set is 254 placements, not 215, and five rounds abort, not six. The second is methodological: the catalogue claims it resolved every record through its own round-and-act table, but no act_tbl exists for R5 Act 2 or R7 Act 2 anywhere in the decompiled source, covering 4,848 placements (17.8% of the corpus), and 177 only reproduces under an undisclosed fallback to those rounds' Act 1 tables. errors_found: RANK 5 (ball), WRONG ZONE - the single most damaging behaviour error. The catalogue says 'PLAYSUB.C:873 raises the horizontal floor from 2560 to 3328 when stageno.b.h==5, which is Wacky Workbench'. build/audit/source/src/LOADER2.C:36-37 defines the mapping: `round = StageNo.b.h + 1; if (round > 1) ++round;`. So stageno.b.h 0,1,2,3,4,5,6 = rounds 1,3,4,5,6,7,8. stageno.b.h==5 is ROUND 7, Stardust Speedway - not Wacky Workbench (which is stageno.b.h==4). This is corroborated: every stageno.b.h==6 test in the source (RING.C:230, ITEM.C:239/273/335/390, SAVE.C:43, FCOL.C:797) reads userflag.b.l, and the only round whose records carry a non-zero secondary byte on ids 16 and 25 is R8 - so 6==R8, hence 5==R7. Consequence: the catalogue's adjudication of disagreement #7 ('Wacky Workbench is stage index 5... R6's reading is the useful one') is backwards, and an implementer following rank 5 would apply the 3328 floor to R6 (68 ball placements) and leave 2560 in R7 (784 ball placements, the largest ball population in the game). The named fix lands on the wrong zone.

RECOMMENDED_FIRST_SLICE INFRASTRUCTURE IS UNDER-SPECIFIED. The catalogue prescribes 'a per-ROUND-and-ACT id-to-handler table' and says 'Per-act is not optional'. The act_tbl is per round, per act AND PER ERA. I parsed all 25 act_tbl arrays and diffed the era variants: R1 Act 1 - ACT11A vs ACT11B differ at 8 ids (id 19 is `marker` in A but `noact` in B, where marker moves to id 43; id 42 kasoku->noact; id 44 hoshi->noact; id 47 emie1->noact; id 48 heart1->noact; id 50 noact->eda). R4 Act 1 - ACT41A/41B/41C differ at 20 ids (id 51 `walls` in A and B, `noact` in C; id 64 is `ring4` in C only - a second ring routine; id 36 `lrblk4` in B only; id 82 `movie4` in B only). R4 Act 2 - ACT42A/42B/42C differ at 19 ids, and ACT42C is only 80 entries long against ACT42A's 82, so ids 81 and 82 do not exist in the Future table at all. R3 Act 1 - ACT31A vs ACT31B differ at 6 ids. A table keyed on (round, act) mis-dispatches every one of these.

RANK 6 (marker), FALSE ID CLAIM. 'all seven, id 19 in every act_tbl' is wrong. id 19 is `marker` in only 16 of the 25 act_tbl arrays. It is `noact` in ACT11B, ACT31B and in all seven Act-3 tables (ACT13C, ACT33C, ACT43C, ACT53, ACT63, ACT73, ACT83). In ACT11B (R1 Act 1, Past) the marker routine sits at id 43 instead. By contrast ids 10, 16, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 and 26 ARE identical across all 25 tables - I checked each one - so the error is specific to marker, the one shared type the catalogue happened to get wrong.

RANK 4 (friend), 'the roam-and-ground-follow code transfers unchanged' IS WRONG FOR R4. The catalogue treats R4 as an art difference ('R4 links FRIEND4.C ... so the art differs per round'). build/audit/source/src/R4/FRIEND4.C is a structurally different routine: it exposes m_init/m0move/m1move, with no t_roll, no t_*/p_* pair, and no ground collision anywhere. m1move (line 276-285) advances x by a constant and sets `yposi.w.h = spawn_y + (sin(phase)>>3)` - a sine orbit about the spawn point, i.e. a swimmer in an underwater zone. m0move (line 222-247) orbits a PARENT actor and calls frameout if `tempact->actno != 82` (the projector), so those animals only exist as projector children. R1/R3/R5/R6/R7/R8 all share the t_*/p_* shape, so the claim holds for six rounds and fails for the seventh: 260 of the 1,566 placements the rank claims would spawn hopping land animals where retail has orbiting swimmers. 'effort: small' is not right for R4.

RANK 9 (mosugu), 'the port's handler needs nothing but the id map' IS WRONG. GOAL.C mosug_init (line 575-585) carries a special case: `if (stageno.w == 513 && time_flag == 1)` - stageno.w 513 is b.h=2 (round 4), b.l=1 (act 2), time_flag 1 (Present) - where a mosugu with subtype 0 rewrites its own subtype to 1 and returns uninitialised, then on the next pass only initialises if `divdevwk[0] == 0`. Separately, GOAL.C offset_set (line 698-729) sets the sign's sproffset from a 56-entry table indexed by (round, era) and then `if (stageno.b.h != 3) sproffset |= 32768`, so the art base is per-round-and-era, not one constant. goal_init (GOAL.C:774-776) does the same: `sproffset = 1084; if (stageno.b.h != 0) sproffset |= 128`. Ranks 9-12 are described as 'effectively four table entries'; they are four table entries plus 28 art bases.

RANKS 1 AND 3, 'zero behaviour work' / 'Same converter secondary-byte fix as ring' UNDERSTATES THE R8 SECONDARY BYTE. The catalogue frames the R8 secondary byte purely as a converter guard to relax. It is a live gameplay field in Metallic Madness. RING.C:230-236: in stage 6 the ring copies userflag.b.l and, when non-zero, clears the high bit of sproffset and raises sprpri from 0 to 2. verdicts.summary:
The catalogue survives. I could not refute its core: the 27,286 total, the per-round counts, the 9,082/9,886/4,256 mis-spawn split, the 104 colliding pairs, the four worst collisions, the 965/1024 capacity headroom and the unsorted-layout list all reproduce exactly when I parse the 70 binaries and the 25 act tables myself. The already_implemented flag is right - supported_types[] covers all 36 R1-placed ids with nothing placed-but-unsupported - and I found no type wrongly marked implemented, which was the failure mode I looked hardest for. The behaviour descriptions for ring, spring, item, wall1, wall7 and wall73 check out line for line against RING.C, SPRING.C, ITEM.C, R4/WALL1.C, R7/WALL7.C and R7/WALL73.C, and the GOAL/SIGN label inversion is real.

Four errors would cause real damage. First, stageno.b.h==5 is Stardust Speedway, not Wacky Workbench - LOADER2.C:36-37 maps b.h 0..6 to rounds 1,3,4,5,6,7,8 - so rank 5's one named constant is attributed to the zone with 68 ball placements instead of the one with 784. Second, the act_tbl is per-era as well as per-act, which the prescribed per-(round,act) table cannot express: R4 Act 1's three era tables differ at 20 ids and ACT42C is two entries shorter than ACT42A. Third, rank 6's 'id 19 in every act_tbl' is false - marker is at id 19 in 16 of 25 tables and at id 43 in ACT11B. Fourth, rank 4's 'transfers unchanged' fails for R4: FRIEND4.C is a different routine with sine-orbit motion, a projector parent and no ground collision, covering 260 placements.

Below those: rank 9's mosugu needs more than an id map (a stageno.w==513 special case plus a 28-entry per-round-and-era art table); the R8 secondary byte is a live layer flag in RING.C and ITEM.C rather than just a converter guard; and the converter-abort list misses R6 id 62 entirely, overcounts R6 block6 by 4 while missing that those same 4 are silently mis-decoded, and says six rounds abort when five do.

Score 7: the ranking order, the build-order argument and the warning against a naive gate lift all hold, and the per-era finding strengthens rather than undermines the first slice. But the ball constant, the R4 animals and the marker id claim each need correcting before anyone writes the id table.

stalls.summary:
Zero terrain defects. 18 of the 26 stalls need an object the port does not implement; 8 are limits of the bot, not the data.

The single most important calibration finding: the shipped bot presses Jump for exactly one frame (tools/zone_walk_test.c, `if(stuck>=30 && !(p.flags&2)){buttons|=SCD_JUMP;...}`), and Sonic's jump is variable-height, so it only ever performs a 33px hop. I measured the port's real full jump at 100px by holding the button (mm81A: centre y 1969 -> 1869). A one-line change to hold Jump while rising moves R43C/D from x=501 to x=949 and R83C/D from x=661 to x=725; adding back-off run-ups takes R83C/D to 981 and R41C/D to 1109. Those eight stalls were never terrain.

The other 18 are sealed against every input I could generate. I built five walker variants (held jump, back-off run-ups, progress-triggered jumps, jump spam, spin dash via the port's Down+Jump charge_buffer path) plus a sweep of single well-timed jumps, and also wrote a 4px-cell flood fill that reads the extracted chunk/block/height tables exactly as src/player.c scramapad and build/probe-source/fcol.c scdchk do. Every route also runs with zero objects: src/objects.c:34 zeroes the placement count for any zone != 0.

For each of the 18 the retail act's own object table puts an actor precisely where the gap or lift is needed, which is what you expect when the terrain is right. The record layout was derived from build/audit/source/src/ACTSET.C actnoset/tm_setchk (x:u16, y:u16 with bits 14-15 = flip, a:u8 with bit7 = one-shot and bits 0-6 = act_tbl index + 1, b = subtype, c>>5 = era mask past/present/future, d = secondary), and type ids were resolved through each round's own ACT<r><a>.C act_tbl. Highlights: R73C/D fall through a 128px hole in the lower floor at x=12172..12299 that wall73 (id 43) subtype 3 at (12224,496) fills exactly - WALL73.C's wall7_tbl0 entry 3 is a 128x32 solid block whose top is y=480, the same as the floor either side. R81A-D sit in a 225-cell sealed pocket with a konbea moving platform (id 42) literally inside it at (487,1916). R82A-D sit in a 96px corridor whose launcher is a piston (id 52) at (432,1182), replaced by a spring in the Past. R42A-D have 260px of completely empty terrain at x=250..511 that three stacked wall1 blocks (id 52) are meant to bridge.

On terrain defects specifically: all 70 programs' foreground chunk map, collision index, height map, width map and angle table are byte-equal to the PC reconstruction tables (tools/extract_zone_auto.py:355-365, build/all-zones-extract.json). The one stage-pack part with no PC oracle is the chunk block table. I probed it by comparing every Good/Bad Future terrain pair; they differ by 3-36% across all zones, so R53C-vs-R53D differing is normal Sonic CD era geometry, not extraction damage. I found no case where extracted data disagrees with the retail source.

Two honest caveats. R51C/D and R53D are my weakest calls: the terrain step there is a steep quarter-pipe face that is within jump range on paper, and I classified them missing_object on the strength of a dair5 moving platform (id 48) hovering in otherwise empty air at exactly the needed height - I cannot prove no input sequence climbs the face. And for R42 Present and Past I could not identify the specific lift out of the y=1728 bay; the wall1 platforms across the void upstream are what put the player on a higher tier in the first place.
